en.title: ShoesNet — B2B Wholesale Footwear Marketplace App
en.description: Rebuilt a wholesale footwear operation that relied on a website and WhatsApp into a controlled B2B ordering platform with clear oversight of vendors, products, and orders.
en.problemHeadline: Wholesale operations were constrained by a retail-style storefront
en.problemBody: The business connected footwear factories with wholesale buyers, but the website was designed like a retail store while orders followed wholesale rules: carton quantities, one supplier per order, and negotiated volume pricing. Orders moved to WhatsApp instead of staying in the system, product quality could not be governed consistently, price changes could trigger disputes, and there was no dependable record of what was sold, to whom, or at what price.
en.diagnosisHeadline: The core issue was operational control, not storefront design
en.diagnosisBody: The business needed three controls: who could join the platform, what could be listed, and a fixed record of the commercial terms at the moment an order was submitted. Without those controls, growth increased operational risk instead of creating a more scalable process.
en.systemHeadline: A mobile-first B2B ordering platform with owner-controlled approvals

en.title: Clean Basket — App Growth & Tracking Rebuild (Riyadh, Saudi Arabia)
en.description: Rebuilt measurement and paid social for a Saudi on-demand laundry app, scaling installs and in-app purchases until order volume exceeded available operational capacity.
en.problemHeadline: Broken tracking left campaigns without conversion signals
en.problemBody: Tracking infrastructure was completely broken — no conversion data was flowing from the app to any ad platform. iOS was effectively invisible: SKAdNetwork was not configured, so Apple's attribution framework returned nothing, and in-app events like Add to Cart and Purchase were not mapped to any platform SDK, leaving all campaigns running with zero optimization signal. On top of that, campaigns across all three platforms had no coherent testing framework, no OS segmentation and no platform-specific creative strategy, with budget scattered against no clear performance benchmarks.
en.diagnosisHeadline: Measurement had to be fixed before media could scale
en.diagnosisBody: Measurement infrastructure was the foundation, not a technical detail. Without conversion signal reaching the ad platforms, no amount of budget or creative investment could produce reliable results — so the fix had to be sequenced foundation-first.

en.title: Beautify Me Medical Center — Google Ads Acquisition & Retention (Dubai, UAE)
en.description: Rebuilt Google Ads for a Dubai medical aesthetics clinic by fixing conversion tracking, restructuring campaigns by service, and adding a retention workflow to support consistent appointment bookings.
en.problemHeadline: Broken conversion tracking and no service-level campaign structure
en.problemBody: Two problems defined the account. Conversion tracking was broken — bookings and form submissions were not recording correctly, so the campaign algorithm had no reliable signal to optimize against and budget was being spent without knowing what worked. Campaign architecture was also unstructured: all services were grouped together with no meaningful separation, making it impossible to optimize individual services independently, and there were no negative keyword lists at either service or brand level, leading to wasted spend on irrelevant queries.
en.diagnosisHeadline: A competitive search market required reliable conversion data and service-level segmentation
en.diagnosisBody: Medical aesthetics is one of the most competitive search categories in Dubai — high intent, high CPC and high customer lifetime value. Without accurate conversion signal and service-level segmentation, the account could not compete efficiently or match ad copy to search intent.
